proof.text: White pawns stand on a3 b4 c3 d4 e3 f4 g3 h4 and Black pawns directly above each (a4 b5 c4 d5 e4 f5 g4 h5). Every pawn is blocked head-on; White's rank-3 pawns attack their own rank-4 pawns, White's rank-4 pawns attack a5 c5 e5 g5 (empty), Black's rank-4 pawns attack b3 d3 f3 h3 (empty) and Black's rank-5 pawns attack their own pawns. Only the kings could stand on those empty squares, and a king may not move into check, so no pawn ever moves or takes. Every pawn a king could reach is protected by a pawn behind it, so neither king ever takes, and the squares of the two sides never touch, so neither king can check the other. With no check there is no checkmate (`rules.win`); stalemate is a draw. Mechanically: `labelled/check.py` visits every reachable position (`no_win`) and finds no ending with a winner.
